sections.h2: Who sends and collects the bill
sections.html:
Wayne divides the work between two desks. Tax Administration decides what your property is worth. The Tax Collector sends the bill and receives the money; mail goes to P.O. Box 1495, Goldsboro, NC 27533. Both are reached from the county tax page.

That page links a billings search, rates, forms, maps, relief programs and a list of tax foreclosure sales, which lets you check what you owe before the sign goes up.

  • Collector: balances, payoff letters, payment options
  • Administration: value, appeals, relief applications
  • Register of Deeds in Goldsboro: deeds and deeds of trust

The site also posts downloadable appraisal data and the 2025 schedule of values, which shows the unit prices the appraisers applied to land and buildings.

sections.h2: Wayne County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Goldsboro anchors a county of 122,278 people over 553.92 square miles. There are 55,106 housing units and 47,507 households, and owners hold 61.5% of occupied homes. Rent runs a median $965 a month, and roughly four homes in ten are rentals, which makes landlords a large share of local sellers.

Growth has been slow: 122,623 residents in 2010, then 117,333 in 2020, with the newest estimate 4.2% over 2020. New building has been modest, with 954 permits for 2025. Because 86.1% of residents kept the same address last year, plenty of owners have no recent sale to go by, and the revaluation notice may be the first price signal they have had in years.

The county revalued every parcel as of 2025 and mailed notices in March. Its revaluation page describes a base of more than 64,000 parcels. Revaluation changes assessed value only. The commissioners and city or town boards set rates later, in budget season.

Appraisers compared recent sales, priced the cost to rebuild, and used an income method on commercial parcels. The county did not apply a flat percentage. Its example is two matching 2019 houses that ended up worth different amounts by 2025.

Revaluation notices for Goldsboro houses and for rural Wayne parcels arrive together, but the numbers rarely move in step. Check the land line and the building line separately, since an error in square footage or condition shows up there first.

Wayne is above the 75,000 population line in G.S. 105-286, so the state can require an earlier reappraisal if the sales ratio drifts outside .85 to 1.15.

A reappraisal looks at local sales, so a neighborhood with new construction and steady buyers can move differently from a farm district. Set your notice beside sales on your own street before you decide to contest it.

Fill out the review form that came with your notice and get it to the Tax Office within 30 days of the notice date. An appraiser then looks at it.

When that informal review changes nothing, a second notice lays out the formal hearing in front of the county's Board of Equalization and Review, and the state Property Tax Commission sits above it. Hold on to copies of whatever you send, since the board hearing starts from that same file.

  • Strong evidence: an appraisal, written repair bids, dated damage photos, nearby sales
  • Weak grounds: your ability to pay, or a value already close to market

Outside revaluation years, use the county's non reappraisal year appeals page instead.

Tax calendar for a Wayne County parcel
EventTiming
Owners list propertyAll of January, starting the first business day
Bill comes dueSeptember 1
Interest startsJanuary 6, at 2%
Hearing board startsOpens sometime from the first Monday in April to the first Monday in May
State appeal30 days after the board mails its decision

From February 1 on, interest accrues at three-quarters of one percent a month. Early payment discounts are a local option, so the Tax Collector can tell you whether one is offered.

Homeowners can cut or postpone a bill three ways, and every one begins with Form AV-9 filed with the county assessor. The Department of Revenue's 2026 form lists a $38,800 income cap, with $58,200 applying to the upper circuit breaker band.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: shields $25,000 or half the appraised value, whichever is more (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 off the value, and income does not matter (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Circuit breaker: caps the bill at 4% or 5% of income and defers whatever is left (G.S. 105-277.1B).

File during the January listing season. The assessor has to take applications up to June 1 before the tax year. Anything deferred turns into a lien and is due when the house sells.

sections.h2: If you sell with taxes owed
sections.html:
Wayne's lien attaches every January 1 (G.S. 105-355), and it stays on the house through a sale, which is why the title company settles the balance from your proceeds.

If nobody pays, the county can sue and sell the house at the courthouse (G.S. 105-374), but paying the full amount owed still redeems it until the sale is confirmed. Wayne keeps a tax foreclosure sales page of its own.

Get the payoff in writing from the Tax Collector, and let the closing office know about any deferral or open appeal.

sections.h2: What to ask before you list
sections.html:
• What is owed on the parcel today, and has this year's bill gone out?
  • Does a Goldsboro special assessment or nuisance abatement charge sit on it?
  • Is an appeal of the 2025 value still open?
  • Is a circuit breaker deferral on the account?

Call the Tax Collector, or try the billings search on the Wayne tax site. With an inherited or empty house in Goldsboro or the country, find out who the county shows as owner before anything else.

1. Find your parcel in the billings search and write down the balance and the tax year.
  2. Ask for a written payoff that stays good through closing day.
  3. See whether an appeal or a circuit breaker deferral is attached.
  4. Give the figure to the closing attorney or title company.
  5. Afterward, make sure the tax office has the new owner's name and mailing address.

A cash sale runs through the same checklist, minus the lender's appraisal and underwriting. With those gone, the tax payoff is often the one item with a hard date, so settle the account early.

Wayne mails each bill to the owner of record. When an heir never recorded anything, the late owner can still be on the account, so ask the Tax Collector whose name is listed and where the mail goes.

A rented house and an empty one get the same bill. Add up each year's balance before you settle on a closing date.

Deed history sits with the register of deeds, and the county's real estate search shows parcel details. Used together, they let a buyer or attorney see who really holds title before a contract is signed.

  • Open the parcel in the real estate search
  • Get the payoff on paper
  • Ask who handles the January listing after the sale

faqs.q: What day does interest begin on a Wayne County bill?
faqs.a: January 6. The bill is due September 1, but interest holds off until that January date. It then runs at 2% through February 1 and 3/4 of 1% a month afterward.

faqs.q: How many parcels did Wayne County revalue in 2025?
faqs.a: The county cites more than 64,000 parcels. Owners received notices in March 2025.

faqs.q: Does revaluation set my tax rate?
faqs.a: No. Revaluation updates value. Elected boards set the rate during budget work, and the county tax page links a Tax Rates page.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for the $45,000 veteran exclusion?
faqs.a: A qualifying disabled veteran owner and certain unmarried surviving spouses, with no age or income limit. Apply on Form AV-9 with the assessor, after a county veteran services office completes the VA portion.

faqs.q: Where do I mail a Wayne County tax payment?
faqs.a: Wayne County Tax Collector, P.O. Box 1495, Goldsboro, NC 27533. Online payment is also linked from the county tax page.
